items.q: What is the International Company of Cuban Dances?
items.a: The company was founded in 2022. We are a team of dancers from around Europe who are passionate about traditional Afro-Cuban dances. Our goal is to train and perform the traditional folkloric Cuban dances outside of Cuba. Find out more about our teachers on the About page, and get an impression of our classes on Instagram.

items.q: How can I join the Academy?
items.a: The academy is open to everyone who wants to join us for the first time. You are welcome to continue in the academy if you don't feel ready to perform yet, or if you can't join very regularly. If your main goal is simply to train and become better at Afro-Cuban dances, you can stay as a student of the academy.

items.q: How can I join the Company?
items.a: There is no formal audition day. The audition happens over the course of several training weekends once you have shown an interest in joining: just mention it to Leonardo or one of the members of the organisation. You attend a minimum of three weekends, taking part in the academy classes while the teachers watch you dance and assess your level. After those three sessions the teachers decide whether you join the company or continue in the academy a while longer.

These are not beginner classes. You need prior knowledge of Afro-Cuban dances: Yoruba, Arará, Palo, Makuta, Yuka and Rumba. The training does not cover basic steps or rhythms, so it's best if you have taken at least two years of classes, or have enough basic training to follow along. This applies to both academy and company members.

items.q: I am a teacher, do I have to audition?
items.a: Yes, everyone goes through the same process. We appreciate that many of you have danced for years and are teachers yourselves, but the process has to be fair, so it's the same for everyone.

items.q: Where do the trainings take place?
items.a: In a different European city every month, thanks to the help of our students. Check the Trainings page for the next dates and venues.

Leonardo Moya, Sergio Larrinaga, Arelys Savón and Mireisi Morales, all former dancers of the Conjunto Folklórico Nacional de Cuba, who also trained there. For the 2026–2027 season they are joined by Javier Monier and Federico Nuñez.

items.q: How long are the training weekends?
items.a: About 10 hours of classes over two days. Trainings usually start on Saturday around noon or 1 pm and finish around 5 pm on Sunday, so everyone has time to travel. The full schedule is published one week before each training.

items.q: What do you do during the trainings?
items.a: Usually a combination of chants, Yoruba technique and specific orishas, Palo, Arará and Rumba, plus traditional popular dances such as mambo, cha-cha-chá and son, with live percussion. It varies from weekend to weekend. Company members also rehearse the choreographies for our shows.
We continue to perform our show Raíces Cubanas in different places across Europe, along with smaller performances and festival appearances during the year. We are always open to new opportunities.

items.q: What is the level of commitment for company members?
items.a: Once you are in the company and working towards a performance, we ask you to attend every month (you can miss only one training, or discuss it with the teachers). You commit to learning the choreographies and practising on your own so we make the best use of our time together. Everyone performs in more than one choreography.

items.q: What does it cost and how do I sign up?
items.a: Tickets and ICCD t-shirts are sold on Weezevent. Early-bird tickets are the cheapest, and we always announce until when they are available.

items.q: Do I need to arrange my own accommodation?
items.a: Yes, everyone organises their own travel and accommodation. You're welcome to arrange to travel with other participants privately. If anything special is organised for a weekend, you'll hear about it in our WhatsApp group.

items.q: Who can I contact with more questions?
items.a: Join our WhatsApp group or send us a message on Instagram, we're happy to help.
